question: What is the medical term for an infective bone disease?
explanation: Osteomyelitis specifically refers to the inflammation and infection of the bone and bone marrow caused by invading pathogens. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why is bone infection particularly difficult for the body to clear on its own?

options.A: The rigid and enclosed structure limits immune cell access
options.B: Pathogens in bone are completely immune to all antibiotics
options.C: Bone tissue has no blood supply whatsoever
options.D: Bone marrow actively protects and nurtures invading bacteria

explanation: The hard structure of bone restricts swelling and limits the entry of white blood cells and systemic drugs. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is a sequestrum in the context of bone infection?

options.A: A new layer of living bone formation
options.B: A piece of dead, infected bone tissue
options.C: An accumulation of pus beneath the periosteum
options.D: A blood clot inside the medullary cavity

explanation: A sequestrum is a segment of infected bone that has lost its blood supply and died. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h2)

question: How does an involucrum form during chronic osteomyelitis?

options.A: The periosteum lays down new living bone around the dead tissue
options.B: Adjacent muscles calcify to wall off the infection site
options.C: Cartilage transforms into solid bone to replace the marrow
options.D: Bacteria secrete calcium deposits to build a protective shell

explanation: The periosteum reacts to the inflammation by producing new bone, termed the involucrum, surrounding the sequestrum. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h2)

question: Which bacteria is the most common cause of osteomyelitis overall?
explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is responsible for the vast majority of acute and chronic bone infections. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h3)

question: A patient with sickle cell disease presents with osteomyelitis. Which organism is suspected first?
explanation: Individuals with sickle cell disease have a unique susceptibility to bone infections caused by Salmonella species. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h3)

question: What is a classic sign of chronic osteomyelitis that differs from acute presentation?
explanation: Chronic bone infection frequently establishes draining tracts that intermittently discharge pus through the skin. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h4)

question: Why do patients with osteomyelitis often refuse to move the affected limb?

options.A: The motor nerves are permanently severed by bacteria
options.B: Pathogenic toxins cause immediate muscle wasting
options.C: Rigid muscle spasms paralyze the joint completely
options.D: Increased pressure and inflammation cause severe localized pain

explanation: Inflammatory exudate builds pressure inside the rigid bone, resulting in intense, throbbing pain aggravated by movement. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h4)

question: Which diagnostic method is considered the gold standard for identifying the exact organism in osteomyelitis?
explanation: A bone biopsy allows direct culture and sensitivity testing to isolate the specific pathogen causing the infection. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h5)

question: Why are plain X-rays often unhelpful in the very early stages of acute osteomyelitis?

options.A: Radiation passes straight through infected bone without registering
options.B: Bone density actually increases during early infection phases
options.C: Inflammatory fluid absorbs all X-ray beams completely
options.D: Visible bone destruction requires substantial mineral loss over time

explanation: Radiographic changes do not appear on standard X-rays until a significant portion of bone calcium is depleted. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the typical route of antibiotic administration during the initial phase of osteomyelitis treatment?
explanation: High-dose intravenous antibiotics are necessary initially to achieve therapeutic drug levels within the poorly vascularized bone tissue. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h6)

question: Why must antibiotic therapy for bone infections continue for many weeks?

options.A: Bacteria inside bone divide once every few weeks
options.B: Kidneys excrete these specific drugs instantly
options.C: Poor blood supply to bone makes drug delivery slow and difficult
options.D: Oral medications are completely metabolized in the stomach

explanation: The limited vascular network in bone requires extended treatment durations to ensure complete eradication of the pathogen. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of surgical debridement in bone infection?

options.A: To drain synovial fluid from the joint space
options.B: To fuse the adjacent joint permanently
options.C: To remove necrotic bone and infected tissue
options.D: To replace the entire bone with metal rods

explanation: Debridement physically excises dead bone and infected material that antibiotics cannot successfully penetrate. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h7)

question: What is the clinical purpose of placing antibiotic-impregnated beads into a surgically cleaned bone cavity?

options.A: To stimulate rapid cartilage growth around the infected area
options.B: To provide high local concentrations of medication directly to the site
options.C: To absorb excess blood and prevent internal hemorrhage
options.D: To permanently replace missing bone structure and provide strength

explanation: Antibiotic beads release high local doses of medication directly into the infected area while minimizing systemic side effects. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h7)

question: A patient with osteomyelitis of the tibia prepares for discharge. Which instruction is most critical?

options.A: Stop taking antibiotics as soon as the skin wound looks dry
options.B: Avoid all physical activity for the rest of your life
options.C: Complete all prescribed antibiotics even if you feel completely better
options.D: Apply heat packs to the affected bone three times daily

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early frequently leads to recurrence of the infection and contributes to drug resistance. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h8)

question: Why must the nurse regularly assess neurovascular status in a limb with osteomyelitis?

options.A: Bone infections instantly cause irreversible paralysis of the toes
options.B: Antibiotics directly attack peripheral nerves during infusion
options.C: Patients lose all sensation permanently due to fever
options.D: Swelling and inflammation can compromise circulation and nerve function

explanation: Increased pressure in the tissues can compress blood vessels and nerves, risking ischemia and neurological deficits. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h8)
